subject: Recap + decisions: embedding vector size, batching, auth & routing (ACROSOFT)
messages:
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
To: Jane Park <jane.park@acrosoft.com>
Cc: Dev Patel <dev.patel@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-06-29T16:12:00-07:00
Subject: Follow-up: embeddings sizing, batching, auth & routing (ACROSOFT call recap)

Jane — thanks for the call earlier today. Short recap from my side and a proposal for next technical steps so we can scope the migration and integration work.

Summary of what I heard: 
- AcroSoft currently stores 1536-dim embeddings (proprietary provider).
- Key requirements: minimal downtime during migration, exact/near-exact similarity scores preserved for search reranking, and per-tenant isolation for vectors.
- Operational constraints: single-region hosting (us-west) for data residency, strict request rate limits from their API gateway (burstable but small sustained QPS), and strict key rotation policies.

Questions / decisions we should lock in: 
1) Vector dimension: do you want us to adopt your existing 1536 vectors or re-embed to our recommended dimension?
2) Normalization: confirm whether you currently use L2-normalized vectors or raw dense vectors.
3) Batch sizing for offline migrations and online upserts — need expected throughput and acceptable migration window.
4) Auth model: API keys vs. short-lived OIDC tokens for Private deployment in the VPC.
5) Routing: single region pinned vs. multi-region fallback (we recommend a single-region primary with cross-region read-only fallback).

Proposed immediate next steps: 
- Dev and I will validate model compatibility and provide an SDK snippet for a dry-run upsert and similarity check.
- AcroSoft to share a small sample (we discussed 10k rows) — thank you for offering to attach.
- Technical sync: propose Tue July 1 9:00 AM PT for Dev + your ML ops lead to walk through the sample output and auth flow.

Attachments requested: sample vectors CSV (10k rows), current embedding metadata (dimension, normalization), and any reranker config.

Thanks — I’ll loop in Marissa for procurement cadence once we align on the migration window.

—Karthik
Karthik Iyer
Senior Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
karthik.iyer@redwood.com

From: Jane Park <jane.park@acrosoft.com>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
Cc: ml-ops@acrosoft.com
Date: 2026-06-30T09:03:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Follow-up: embeddings sizing, batching, auth & routing (ACROSOFT call recap)

Thanks Karthik — appreciate the clear recap. A few clarifications and constraints from our side: 

1) Dimension: we are currently at 1536 (we use an internal variant of a public 1536 model). We would prefer to keep the existing vector size if possible to avoid re-embedding the entire corpus.
2) Normalization: our current pipeline L2-normalizes vectors post-encoding (we use cosine similarity).
3) Throughput: the full corpus is ~3.2M documents. We can stage the migration over 2 weeks; nightly batches of up to 200k/24h are acceptable, with an initial dry-run of 10k.
4) Auth: for the VPC deployment we require short-lived tokens (15m) minted by our identity provider; long-lived API keys are allowed for hosted PoC only.
5) Routing: single-region (us-west) is mandatory for writes; reads can failover to eu-west in DR but we prefer primary read locality.

Attaching the sample CSV (acrosoft_existing_vectors.csv) — it includes id, vector (base64), embedding_dim, norm_type, timestamp. Feel free to use a reduced sample for the dry-run.

One more ask: we currently use a scored reranker that expects small differences in cosine similarity to be preserved — any change in numeric precision or quantization must be evaluated.

Happy to meet Tue July 1, 9:00 AM PT — I’ll invite our ML ops lead (cc’d).

Best,
Jane
Jane Park
Head of ML Ops, AcroSoft
jane.park@acrosoft.com

Attachment: acrosoft_existing_vectors.csv (10,000 rows)

From: Dev Patel <dev.patel@redwood.com>
To: Jane Park <jane.park@acrosoft.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-06-30T11:28:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Follow-up: embeddings sizing, batching, auth & routing (ACROSOFT call recap)

Jane — thanks for the sample and the constraints. A few technical notes and a short proposal that should address your preservation and auth requirements.

1) Vector dimension compatibility
- Redwood supports serving models with 1536-dim outputs; we can accept 1536 vectors natively. That avoids re-embedding the full corpus.
- If you ever want to move to a different size for model improvements, we can support a gradual migration pattern (aliasing old namespace + new namespace and shadow-reads).

2) Normalization + similarity preservation
- Keep sending L2-normalized vectors (cosine similarity). Our vector store supports both raw and normalized; for similarity search we will do inner product on L2-normalized vectors which is equivalent to cosine.
- Be mindful of quantization: if you plan to use int8 quantization on storage to reduce footprint, run a fidelity check on a representative prompt set (we can run that during the dry-run).

3) Batching and migration strategy
- For offline migration: we recommend chunked batches of ~50k vectors per job to keep memory and index-update variance reasonable. With your 200k/night window, we can kick off 4 concurrent jobs of 50k each with backoff on throttling.
- For online upserts during transition: use idempotent upsert with checksum field (we suggest SHA256 of source text) so duplicate processing is safe.

4) Auth and token flow
- For Private (VPC) deployment we will support your short-lived tokens. Pattern: your IDP mints a signed JWT; Redwood-side service validates via JWKS and issues a short-lived internal session for request routing. We will provide a sample OIDC token exchange snippet in the SDK.
- For hosted PoC we can use API keys (limited scope).

5) Routing and model variant selection
- Writes: pin to us-west primary (no cross-region writes).
- Reads: configurable fallback to eu-west in case of regional outage; we keep routing at the request-level and expose a per-route SLO.

6) Reranker preservation
- We'll run a fidelity comparison during the dry-run: compute cosine on your existing vectors and on vectors served by Redwood (if you elect re-embedding). For storage quantization, we'll generate delta distributions and present AUC/drop metrics.

Attached is a sample SDK snippet and a sample schema: redwood_embed_sample_schema.json (contains field names, id, vector_base64, embed_dim, norm_type, checksum). Also linking a short doc: https://docs.google.com/document/d/1aBcExampleDriveLink

If that looks good, I will prepare a minimal PoC runbook and a small test job you can execute from your environment (we’ll provide terraform + job manifest).

—Dev
Dev Patel
Principal Engineer, Inference Integrations, Redwood Inference
dev.patel@redwood.com

Attachment: redwood_embed_sample_schema.json

Jane — great to see alignment on the technical front. A couple of commercial / timeline notes from my side: 

- Procurement: we will prepare an initial PoC SOW that covers the dry-run (10k) + a staged migration plan (2-week window). I’ll share a draft by EOD Friday.
- Success metrics: preserve top-K reranker AUC within 0.5% and 99th percentile similarity error under 0.02 (we’ll lock numbers during the PoC).
- Pricing: PoC usage can be covered under trial credits; migration and sustained usage will be part of a reserved capacity conversation.

Next steps I’m tracking:
1) Dev to publish SDK snippet + runbook (in progress).
2) Karthik to run the dry-run coordination Tue 7/1 9:00 AM PT.
3) Jane to confirm invite and any additional attendees from ML Ops.
4) Marissa to share PoC SOW draft by 7/3.

Looking forward to the sync.

—Marissa

Subject: Confirmed: Tue 7/1 09:00 AM PT dry-run + deliverables

All — quick confirmation after the sync this morning. Agreed items and owners: 

- Dimension: keep 1536 (owner: AcroSoft / Jane).
- Normalization: continue sending L2-normalized vectors; Redwood will store as-is and run inner-product search for cosine equivalence (owner: Dev).
- Dry-run: 10k sample from Jane was used; Dev ran a fidelity test and will share the report by EOD 7/2 (owner: Dev).
- Migration window: staged nightly batches up to 200k/night; recommended chunk size 50k/job (owner: AcroSoft + Redwood ops).
- Auth: use short-lived OIDC tokens in Private deployment; Dev to provide OIDC exchange code snippet and SDK example (owner: Dev).
- Routing: writes pinned to us-west; reads can failover to eu-west read-only (owner: Redwood infra).
- Commercial: Marissa to send PoC SOW draft by 7/3 and confirm credits (owner: Marissa).

Related artifacts: https://docs.google.com/document/d/1aBcExampleDriveLink (dry-run plan), HubSpot deal record https://app.hubspot.com/deal/1234567

If any of the owners above need to adjust assumptions, please reply-all with corrections. Otherwise we’ll proceed with the runbook and Dev will kick off the fidelity job.

Thanks — see you on the runbook updates.

—Karthik
